decision: Reject worker heartbeat intervals that are non-positive or greater than or equal to the mission lease before opening coordinator storage.
problem: WorkerRuntime.open previously accepted a heartbeat interval that could be equal to or longer than leaseMs. In that configuration the first automatic heartbeat could occur only after authority had already expired, creating avoidable stale-worker failures before any Qubes transport is involved.

reviews.correctness: Preferred fail-before-claim validation tied directly to leaseMs. A worker configuration that cannot renew before expiry is invalid by construction and should never touch durable state.
reviews.robustness_security: Preferred fail-closed validation rather than silently clamping the requested interval. Silent clamping hides deployment mistakes and makes the effective authority policy differ from configuration.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Preferred one local numeric check over an external watchdog, heartbeat daemon, longer leases, or extra coordinator round trips. The selected approach adds no worker network/Qubes traffic and negligible CPU or memory cost.

alternatives_rejected: Silently clamp heartbeatIntervalMs below leaseMs: masks unsafe configuration and creates configuration/runtime drift.
Lengthen leaseMs automatically: changes failure detection and reclaim latency globally instead of fixing the invalid heartbeat policy.
Add a separate heartbeat daemon now: stronger isolation from event-loop stalls but materially larger lifecycle, IPC, credential, and regression surface for Slice 1.
qa: heartbeatIntervalMs == leaseMs is rejected before coordinator storage I/O.
Existing automatic-heartbeat long-running worker and stale-token fencing regressions remain in test:mission-runtime.
The new regression test is included in full mission-runtime QA and is a workflow path trigger.
failure_lessons: Lease fencing is only useful if the renewal schedule is itself valid relative to the lease lifetime.
Configuration validation should occur before durable state is opened or claimed whenever invalid policy can be determined locally.
Event-loop starvation remains a separate risk; this change prevents misconfiguration but does not claim to make synchronous CPU-bound execution heartbeat-safe.
remaining_risks: A JavaScript event-loop stall longer than the lease can still delay the automatic heartbeat even with a valid interval.
Real-worker readiness still requires executable QA plus Qubes transport qualification using the same lease-token semantics.
